sets.title: Everyday look-alikes 1
sets.intro: These very common English words look like Spanish words, but they mean something different. Read each note, then practice the English word for each meaning.

learn.def: Not 'asistir'. 'Asistir' = to attend / go to.
learn.example: The nurse will assist you with your bag.

learn.def: Not 'excitado'. Use 'excited' for happy energy about something good.
learn.example: The kids are excited about the trip.

learn.def: Not 'constipado'. 'Constipado' = having a cold.
learn.example: He feels constipated, so he eats more fruit.

learn.def: Not 'desierto'. 'Desierto' = desert.
learn.example: We had chocolate cake for dessert.

learn.def: Not 'argumento'. 'Argumento' = reason or plot.
learn.example: They had an argument about money.

learn.def: Not 'idioma'. 'Idioma' = language.
learn.example: 'It's raining cats and dogs' is an idiom.

learn.def: Not 'gente'. 'Gente' = people.
learn.example: The doctor has a gentle voice.

learn.def: Not 'raro'. 'Raro' = strange or weird.
learn.example: A white tiger is very rare.

learn.def: Not 'ordinario'. 'Ordinario' = rude or vulgar.
learn.example: It was an ordinary day at work.

learn.def: Not 'extranjero'. 'Extranjero' = foreigner.
learn.example: Don't talk to strangers at night.

sets.title: Free time and culture look-alikes
sets.intro: These words are about shows, books and events. They look like Spanish words, but the English meaning is different.

learn.def: Partly 'función'. In English, 'function' means purpose or how something works. A 'function' can also be a formal event. For a movie 'función', say 'showing' or 'screening'.
learn.example: What is the function of this button?

learn.def: Not 'editorial' (publishing house). In English, an 'editorial' is a newspaper article that gives the opinion of the newspaper. A 'publisher' is the company that prints books.
learn.example: The editorial says the city needs more parks.

learn.es: encuentro de personas que se separaron
learn.def: Not 'reunión' (a meeting). In English, a 'reunion' is a party when people meet again after many years. A 'reunión' at work is a 'meeting'.
learn.example: We had a family reunion last summer.

learn.def: Not 'exposición' (exhibit). In English, an 'exposition' is a clear explanation of an idea. An art 'exposición' is an 'exhibition' (or 'exhibit').
learn.example: The book gives a clear exposition of the theory.

learn.def: Not 'balón' (ball). In English, a 'balloon' is a rubber bag filled with air or gas: 'globo'. A football is a 'ball'.
learn.example: The children blew up red balloons for the party.

learn.def: Not exactly 'audiencia' (court hearing or a formal meeting). In English, the 'audience' is the group of people who watch a show or listen. For a court 'audiencia', say 'hearing'.
learn.example: The audience clapped for a long time.

learn.def: Not exactly 'espectáculo' (any show). In English, a 'spectacle' is an impressive or strange sight. 'Spectacles' (plural) are old-fashioned glasses. A theater or TV 'espectáculo' is a 'show'.
learn.example: The fireworks were a spectacle.

learn.def: Not 'idioma' (language). In English, an 'idiom' is a fixed phrase with a special meaning, like 'it's raining cats and dogs'. For 'idioma', say 'language'.
learn.example: 'Break a leg' is an idiom that means good luck.

learn.def: Not only 'crónica' (a column in a newspaper). In English, a 'chronicle' is a long record of events in time order. A short 'crónica' in a newspaper is a 'column' or 'report'.
learn.example: The book is a chronicle of life in the town.

learn.def: Not only 'fabricar' (to make). In English, to 'fabricate' usually means to invent something false, like a story. For 'fabricar', say 'make' or 'manufacture'.
learn.example: He fabricated a story about his weekend.

learn.def: 'Caravan' = a vehicle you live in on holiday (UK), or a group of travelers. A line of stopped cars = traffic jam.

learn.def: 'Rare' = not common. Not 'raro' (strange). Strange = strange / weird.

sets.title: Law and official matters
sets.intro: Legal words have many false friends. Learn the real meaning so you can read the news and official papers correctly.

learn.def: Not 'instancia' (a formal request). 'Instance' = an example or one case. A formal request = request / application.
learn.example: This is an instance of bad service.

learn.def: 'Audience' = people who watch or listen. Not 'audiencia' (a court meeting). A court meeting = hearing.
learn.example: The audience clapped for a long time.

learn.def: Not 'fiscal' (a lawyer who accuses). 'Fiscal' = about taxes and public money. The lawyer who accuses = prosecutor.
learn.example: The government's fiscal year starts in January.

learn.def: 'Process' = a series of steps. A court case = trial / lawsuit. Spanish 'proceso' can also mean a trial.
learn.example: The process to get a visa takes six weeks.

learn.def: Not 'defensor' (the lawyer). 'Defendant' = the person accused in a court case. The lawyer = defense lawyer.
learn.example: The defendant said he was innocent.

learn.def: Not 'probar' (to try or to taste). 'Probe' = investigate deeply. To show something is true = prove.
learn.example: Police started a probe into the bank robbery.

learn.def: Not 'asalto' (a robbery). 'Assault' = a physical attack on a person. A robbery = robbery / hold-up.
learn.example: He was arrested for assault.

learn.def: Not 'policía' (police). 'Policy' = rules of a company or an insurance contract. The people who catch criminals = police.
learn.example: The company policy says no phones in meetings.

learn.def: Not 'molestar' (to bother). 'Molest' = a crime: to attack or abuse a person. To bother = bother / disturb.
learn.example: The police arrested a man for molesting a young woman.

learn.def: 'Evidence' = facts or objects that help prove something in court. Not 'evidencia' (something very clear). Very clear = obvious.
learn.example: The police found new evidence at the crime scene.

learn.def: Partial friend. 'Constitución' = the basic law of a country. 'Constitution' = that law, and also a person's general health and strength ('a strong constitution').

learn.def: Partial friend. 'Gabinete' = a small office or a government team. 'Cabinet' = the group of senior ministers, or a cupboard for storing things.

learn.def: Not 'demandar'. 'Demandar' = to sue someone in court. 'Demand' = to ask very strongly, as if you have the right. To sue is 'to sue'.
learn.example: The workers demand better pay.

learn.def: Not 'resignar'. 'Resignarse' = to accept a bad situation. 'Resign' = to leave a job or position on purpose.
learn.example: The minister resigned after the scandal.

learn.def: Not 'probar' (to taste, to try). 'Prove' = to show with facts that something is true. To taste is 'to try' or 'to taste'.
learn.example: Scientists proved that the theory was true.

learn.def: Partial friend. 'Régimen' = a diet or a system of government. 'Regime' = a government, often one that is not democratic. A diet is 'a diet'.
learn.example: The old regime ended after the revolution.

learn.def: Partial friend. 'Intriga' = secret plans or a plot. 'Intrigue' (verb) = to make someone very curious. As a noun it means secret plans to get power.
learn.example: The strange letter intrigued me.

learn.def: Partial friend. 'Conferencia' = a talk or lecture (also a phone call: 'conferencia'). 'Conference' = a big meeting where people from one field come together. A single talk is 'a lecture' or 'a talk'.

learn.def: Not 'abogado' (lawyer). 'Advocate' (noun) = a person who publicly supports an idea. As a verb it means to support publicly. A lawyer is 'a lawyer' or 'an attorney'.
learn.example: She is an advocate for children's rights.

learn.def: Not 'disputar' (to compete for something). 'Dispute' = a serious disagreement, or to say that something is not true. To compete is 'to compete'.
learn.example: They had a dispute about the land.

learn.def: Not 'gentil' (kind, polite). 'Gentle' = soft, careful and not rough. 'Gentil' in Spanish is closer to 'kind' or 'polite'.

learn.def: Spanish 'vulgar' = common and ordinary. English 'vulgar' = rude and in bad taste. For the Spanish sense, say 'common' or 'ordinary'.

learn.def: Not 'preservativo' (condom). 'Preservative' = a substance added to food so it lasts longer. A condom is a 'condom'.

learn.def: Not 'crudo' (raw). 'Crude' = rude, or very simple and not carefully made. 'Raw' = not cooked.
learn.example: He made a crude joke at dinner.

learn.def: Not 'idioma' (language). 'Idiom' = a phrase whose meaning is different from its words, such as 'break a leg'. A language is 'a language'.
learn.example: 'Break a leg' is a famous idiom.

learn.def: Not 'extraño' (strange). 'Stranger' = a person you do not know. 'Stranger' is also the comparative of 'strange'.

learn.def: Not 'genial' (brilliant). 'Genial' in English = friendly and kind in a warm way. Brilliant is 'brilliant' or 'great'.
learn.example: The host was a genial man who made everyone feel welcome.

learn.def: Not 'decente' (clean, respectable). 'Decent' = of a good enough standard, or fair. 'Decent' also means respectable.
